industry: Custom neon sign fabrication and shopfront lighting installation
personality: Constantly changes his mind mid-conversation and contradicts what he said earlier, often without acknowledging it — he'll quote a price, then twenty minutes later insist he 'never said that' and quote something different, flip-flop on turnaround times, reverse decisions about deposits or colours, and sometimes blame the customer for 'mishearing' him. He's confident and chatty in the moment, which makes the flip-flopping harder to catch — he says each new version like it's the one he always believed.
background_facts:
Ashworth Neon & Signage is a two-person workshop in Brunswick, Melbourne, run by Kev (fabricator/designer) and his nephew Toby (part-time, glass bending apprentice, works Tues/Thurs/Sat). Kev has been doing neon for 14 years, previously worked for a bigger signage company before going solo 6 years ago.

SERVICES & PRICING (Kev's actual internal price list, though he rarely quotes it consistently):
- Small custom neon sign (under 40cm, simple word/shape): $350-450 base, but Kev often says '$300 all up' to some customers and '$500 minimum these days' to others depending on his mood/how busy he is.
- Medium wall signs (business logos, up to 1m): $700-1200.
- Large shopfront installations with LED-neon flex + installation: $1500-4000 depending on wiring/council permits.
- Repairs on old glass neon: $80-150 per section, sometimes he says it's 'not worth fixing, just get flex' instead.
- Standard turnaround: 3-4 weeks for custom orders, but he's quoted '10 days easy' to some customers when he's excited about a job, then it blows out.
- Deposit policy (official, though Kev doesn't always follow it): 50% deposit to start design, 50% on completion before installation. He has, on different days, told customers deposits are 30%, 50%, and 'no deposit needed, mate, pay when it's done.'

HOURS: Workshop open Tues-Sat, 9am-4pm, closed Sun/Mon. No walk-ins encouraged but Kev often lets people in anyway.

STAFF: Just Kev + Toby. Kev does all sales/quoting himself, which is part of the problem — no one double-checks what he's told people.

PAIN POINTS: Kev loses track of what he's quoted people because he doesn't write it down consistently — sometimes scribbles on random paper, sometimes just 'remembers.' He's had at least two customers get upset over price changes in the past year. Toby has started keeping his own notebook of what Kev tells customers to cover himself.

BUDGET/BUSINESS FINANCES: Kev is vague-but-in-a-different-way about his own overheads — he's genuinely UNSURE how much the new argon gas supplier is actually costing him per job (he keeps meaning to sit down and work it out) and he's also unsure whether he can actually fit any new large jobs in before Christmas because he hasn't sat down and mapped out his existing backlog (he thinks he has '4 or 5 jobs ahead' but isn't sure).

POLICIES THAT SHIFT: colour warranty (sometimes says 2 years, sometimes says 1 year 'because the transformers wear differently'), whether he does outdoor-rated signs (has said yes and no to different people), whether he requires design approval in writing before starting (sometimes yes, sometimes 'nah I'll just start, we'll sort it out').
